record.paper_title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
record.original_question: Which infinite mathematical structures have a direct analogue of Ramsey's theorem? Here a direct analogue means that, for finite colorings of the relevant finite substructures of the infinite structure, one can find an isomorphic infinite substructure on which all those finite substructures are monochromatic, as happens for k-element subsets of the natural numbers and for k-uniform complete hypergraphs on infinitely many vertices.

evidence.quote: Theorem 1.1 (Ramsey, [58]). Given positive integers k and r and a coloring of the k-element subsets of the natural numbers N into r colors, there is an infinite set of natural numbers N ⊆ N such that all k-element subsets of N have the same color.
Question 1.2. Which infinite structures carry an analogue of Ramsey’s Theorem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Ramsey's theorem states that for all positive integers k and r, every coloring of the k-element subsets of the natural numbers N with r colors admits an infinite subset M ⊆ N such that all k-element subsets of M receive the same color. An analogous statement holds for k-uniform complete hypergraphs on a countably infinite vertex set: every finite coloring of the k-edges admits an infinite induced sub-hypergraph that is monochromatic.

Call this property a "direct Ramsey analogue" for an infinite structure A in a fixed relational (or functional) language: for every finite substructure type F (i.e., every isomorphism type of finite substructure of A) and every coloring of the copies of F in A with finitely many colors, there exists a substructure A' ⊆ A isomorphic to A such that all copies of F inside A' receive the same color.

Problem. Characterize the infinite structures A which carry a direct Ramsey analogue, i.e., determine necessary and sufficient conditions on A under which, for every finite substructure type F and every finite coloring of the copies of F in A, there is an isomorphic copy of A inside A on which all copies of F are monochromatic.
artifact.category_tag: Structural Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures
artifact.status_search_result: The question of which infinite structures admit a direct Ramsey analogue is a central, broad open problem in structural Ramsey theory. Known results show that most homogeneous structures (e.g., the rationals, the Rado graph, Henson graphs) fail to have a literal direct analogue but admit finite "big Ramsey degrees"; characterizing all infinite structures with a direct Ramsey property (degree exactly 1 for every finite substructure) remains open and is actively investigated, as reflected in recent surveys such as the 2024 survey on big Ramsey structures.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Concentrates on big Ramsey degrees, presenting their essential structure where known and outlining areas for further development.
status_evidence.claim: The question of which infinite structures carry an analogue of Ramsey's theorem motivates an active research program on big Ramsey degrees, with many cases unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A survey on big Ramsey structures
status_evidence.snippet: In recent years, there has been much progress... all known examples of infinite structures with finite big Ramsey degrees have a single expansion called a big Ramsey structure.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey shows the general classification problem is still being actively studied with open subquestions.
